Teamwork (inc Sportsmanship)
Welcome
The Chandler is a Church of England Junior School at the heart of two village communities – Milford and Witley – in the Surrey Hills.
Our very first priority is to ensure that our children and staff are safe so that they are in the best possible position to learn. You can read our Safeguarding policy here.
Our Christian ethos underpins our ambition to best prepare each child to fulfil their potential in the wider world as a successful citizen of the future. We place a strong emphasis on community and have adopted a Values based curriculum, teaching a different Value each month.

New Starters
Welcome to our school community! We are thrilled to have you and your family join us and look forward to partnering with you in your child’s educational journey. At our school, we are committed to providing a safe, nurturing, and engaging environment where every student can grow academically, socially, and emotionally. We value open communication and strong family involvement, and we believe that together, we can help your child thrive. We’re excited to get to know you and work together to make this a successful and enriching experience for your family. Welcome aboard!

pageCache.pageTitle: The Chandler CofE Junior School - Music Lessons
pageCache.text:
Music Lessons
At The Chandler, the children have the opportunity to take part in music both in school in their class lessons, and in other ways such as in the school choir.
The children can also have instrumental music lessons in school which are run by external providers. We have a number of teachers who come into school to deliver the lessons during the school day.
Currently we have three providers who come into school as listed below. To find out more please check out their websites or contact them directly (see below) for more information and to book/pay for lessons.
The Music Works offer a range of music tuition. Currently they teach drum, guitar, keyboard, singing and band skills lessons at The Chandler. For more information, visit their website The Music Works
The Music Works flyer
Keith Ryder - Guitar & Ukelele lessons
A professional musician and songwriter, Keith offers lessons in contemporary guitar and ukelele. Spaces are available for new pupils - beginners are very welcome. Keith may be contacted on: 01483 414874 or 07958 534458, or by emailing keith.ryder@btinternet.com.
Surrey Arts are very pleased to offer children the opportunity to have music lessons, covering a wide range of instruments. The recommended age for instrumental teaching will vary depending on the instrument. Please see When you can learn to play an instrument and what instruments we hire for information. At present, they provide tuition in clarinet and saxophone at The Chandler.
To sign up please apply here - Registration - Surrey Arts (speedadmin.dk)
For more information, please contact surreyartsmusic@surreycc.gov.uk
Surrey Arts are keen that all pupils, no matter their background or financial situation feel able to learn an instrument with us. They offer, subject to lesson availability, free group lessons and instrument hire for those who qualify for free school meals, registered Surrey Young Carers and looked after children, and also work with several charities to help those who may need financial help but don’t qualify for the above support. Full details of concessions and financial assistance can be found here: Apply and pay for children's music lessons - Surrey County Council (surreycc.gov.uk)

pageCache.text:
Clubs
We are keen to encourage children to participate in clubs, which can often complement their academic work, and broaden their sphere of activities. Clubs run all year round at lunchtime as well as before and after school - some of the clubs which have been available recently are:
The timetable of externally-run clubs for this term can be found here:
Autumn 2026 Club Timetable
To book a club, please contact the provider directly using the contact details in the following flyers:
The Outdoors Project
Musical Theatre Autumn 2026
Waverley Athletics Booking Form
School’s Out!
At The Chandler we host a very popular extended hours club called ‘School’s Out.’ It is run by Mrs Butterfield and provides children with a range of fun activities – both before the day begins (from 8.00 a.m.) and after the school day (until 6.00 p.m.).
Children can be booked in for regular or one-off sessions.
If you are interested in signing your child up for School's Out, please complete the form below and return it to Mrs Butterfield on schoolsout@chandlerjunior.school or leave it with the school office for her attention.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Chandler CofE Junior School - Report An Absence
pageCache.text:
Report An Absence
If you need to report your child’s absence from school for illness or any other unavoidable cause, please do so via the Studybugs mobile phone app. Please click here to get the free and secure app now.
Alternatively, you can go to http://studybugs and report your child’s absence via their website.
If you are unable to access the internet, please phone the School Office on 01428 683071 and follow the instructions.
Absences should be reported by 9.00 a.m. on each and every day that a child is not in school.
We are required by law to record “unauthorised" absences or frequent latecomers, and any absence from school is considered "unauthorised" until we receive an explanation via email or phone call from a parent/carer.
Leave of absence
To request a planned leave of absence from school (e.g. holiday), parents/carers must complete a “Request for Leave of Absence Form” (see below - a copy is also available from the School Office). The completed form should be submitted to school at least 2 weeks prior to the first day of absence.
Request for Leave of Absence Form
We would like to refer you to the revised rules on attendance, unauthorised absences, and penalty fines, which apply from 19 August 2024 and are set out in this letter:
Attendance letter to parents September 2024

pageCache.pageTitle: The Chandler CofE Junior School - PE Lessons
pageCache.text:
PE Lessons
Children come into school in PE kit on their PE days. For the academic year 2025/26, these are as follows:
Year 3 - Mondays and Thursdays
4H - Wednesdays and Thursdays
4P and 4S - Tuesdays and Wednesdays
Year 5 - Tuesdays and Fridays
Year 6 - Mondays and Thursdays
PE Kit
PE kit is to be worn in to school on PE days (and only on PE days).
*Chandler School PE T-shirt, in House Colour £6.50
*Red Chandler School PE Hoodie (optional), £13.50 (plain) / £15 (with embroidered logo)
Otherwise a Red Chandler School sweatshirt or cardigan as above
Note – no other jumpers or hoodies allowed
Plain black or navy shorts, skorts, leggings or joggers (no stripes or logos)
Note – no other colours allowedPlain socks/trainer socks
* only available from Price and Buckland
Long Hair
Shoulder length or longer hair (boys and girls) must be tied back neatly. Children who do not have their hair tied back will be provided with a hairband or elastic band.
Earrings
Children with pierced ears may wear one small stud earring in each earlobe (hoops or dangly earrings are not permitted). However, the earrings must be removed for sport and PE activities. For this reason, children must be able to remove their earrings themselves – if they are unable to do so, please remove the earrings before school on PE days.
Watches
Watches may be brought into school, but please ensure that they are CLEARLY MARKED and handed to the class teacher for all PE and games lessons. Smart watches are treated in the same way as mobile phones.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Chandler CofE Junior School - Transport
pageCache.text:
Transport
Surrey County Council, in accordance with its statutory duty, will provide free home to school travel assistance for children of compulsory school age to the nearest available school from their home address who meet the 'qualifying distance' criteria which are:
Distances will be measured from the address point of the pupil's house, to either the nearest school gate available for pupils to use when measuring to a Surrey school, or the address point of the school property when measuring to a school outside Surrey.
Applications can be made following the below link: Apply for under 16 travel assistance to school - Surrey County Council (surreycc.gov.uk).
Below is the link explaining more about Surrey County Council Home to School Transport.
https://www.surreycc.gov.uk/schools-and-learning/schools/transport
All queries regarding transport should be directed to Surrey County Council in the first instance:
www.surreycc.gov.uk/schools-and-learning/schools/transport/contact-us
Cycling
We want to encourage children to cycle safely to school. We have storage space in our cycle racks to accommodate bicycles. Children may cycle to school with an adult, or if parents/carers are confident in their child's ability to cycle unaccompanied, they may cycle alone with written parental permission.
Cyclists must wear a helmet. The school accepts no liability for loss or damage to any bicycles or equipment left on school premises.
We support the Surrey County Council Bikeability courses for years 4 and 6 and aim to offer these within school where possible.

pageCache.text:
Collective Worship & Religious education
Collective Worship is an important opportunity for the school family to come together. It is a chance for us all to gather to reflect upon a whole host of issues affecting our world and to learn about the Values we have adopted as children of God in our community.
As a church school we believe it is important to engage with the spiritual side of life.
Collective Worship
On Mondays to Thursdays, collective worship takes place at 10.10 a.m. for 20 minutes. On most Fridays we come together at 2.45 p.m, often to celebrate with a class assembly (parents are welcome to come to these - please see the school calendar for when these are scheduled).
Monday – Led by the HeadteacherTuesday – Singing togetherWednesday – Led by class teachersThursday – Led by our local clergy
Parents have the right to withdraw their child from religious worship but, as a church school, we would discourage this. It is also an important time for whole school issues to be discussed and for messages to be given out. Parents must inform the Chair of Governors and Headteacher in writing if they wish to withdraw their child.
We welcome parents who join us for class assemblies, and for some of the special events throughout the year.
Religious Education
As a Church School we believe Religious Education is critical in developing an understanding of self and of the World. Much of our work is Christian based and linked to our exciting assemblies and visits to the local church. Children also learn about other religions in order to compare Christianity with other faiths. Parents may have their child withdrawn from specific religious teachings and collective worship, if they so wish by writing to the Headteacher. However, we would discourage this.
The link below will take you to the Surrey agreed syllabus for Religious education (2023-2028)
Surrey Agreed Syllabus for RE
The syllabus has been constructed to help schools to sequence the RE curriculum in a way that is coherent, uses multi-disciplinary skills and builds pupils’ knowledge.
In addition, the syllabus helps pupils to understand their own and others’ worldviews, religious and non-religious, and appreciate the influences of these on everyday life.

pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to The Chandler.
I am Hugh Rawson, Headteacher, and I look forward to sharing our school with you through this website.
We were graded Good by Ofsted in their most recent inspection of January 2023.
The Chandler is a Church of England Junior School at the heart of two village communities – Milford and Witley – in the Surrey Hills.
Our very first priority is to ensure that our children and staff are safe so that they are in the best possible position to learn. You can read our Safeguarding policy here.
Our Christian ethos underpins our ambition to best prepare each child to fulfil their potential in the wider world as a successful citizen of the future. We place a strong emphasis on community and have adopted a Values based curriculum, teaching a different Value each month.
Our outstanding pastoral care, and an environment in which all can flourish, ensures that each child’s strengths and abilities are recognised and celebrated.
We believe that every child is special – made in the image of God – and learns best when they are happy and secure. Our outstanding pastoral care, and an environment in which all can flourish, ensures that each child’s strengths and abilities are recognised and celebrated.
Learning is brought to life through active, first-hand experiences, with children enjoying a rich, broad and varied curriculum. We have lots of space for learning and play in our well-equipped building and fabulous grounds, and we make full use of these. Whenever we can, we take learning out into the wider world – be it on our doorstep or further afield. Throughout the year, special occasions, themed days and weeks further enrich our curriculum and enliven learning.
Children are given opportunities to shine in sporting events, class assemblies, school productions, musical performances and many other areas. A wide range of clubs and extra-curricular activities provide plenty for the children to choose from – football, netball, gymnastics, athletics, judo, gardening, inventors, cooking, Lego and crafts to name a few.
Alongside our excellent PE curriculum and healthy school meals, every child has the opportunity to develop both educationally and physically to the best of their ability. We are working closely with The Music Works to enable every child to have the best possible opportunities to access quality music provision – be they learning, listening, making, composing or performing. It’s a very exciting project which is already impacting upon our whole community – creating confident, expressive and creative learners.
Hugh Rawson | Headteacher & Designated Safeguarding Lead

medicines
In line with local authority guidance, all medicines to be administered in school should be accompanied by written instructions from the parent and/or doctor specifying the type of medicine, the circumstances under which it should be given, the frequency and dosage levels. A form is available from the School Office for parents/carers to fill in if their child needs medication, or can be printed off from here:
Medication Request Form
Any medicine brought into school must be brought in and collected by the parent and should be in clearly labelled containers including: child’s name, the type of medicine and dosage instructions.
Where possible, it would be helpful if medication can be prescribed in dose frequencies which will enable it to be taken outside of school hours. Parents/carers are encouraged to consult their doctor or dentist about this.
Children must not carry medicine to and from school. The only exceptions to this may be inhalers or travel sickness medication (for use on educational visits).
Inhalers must be carried on children at all times. Please ensure that all inhalers are clearly marked with your child’s name.

pageCache.text:
PTA - The Friends
Who are we?
The Friends are the equivalent of The Chandler PTA – we are a friendly and informal group who organise fundraising and social events throughout the year.
All The Chandler staff, parents and carers are automatically Friends, but anyone who is interested in supporting the children and the school is welcome to get involved – this includes staff, grandparents, family members, etc.
What do we do?
The Friends are a crucial part of fundraising for the school and they make a huge difference to funds to ensure school improvements. Your donations help us provide the little extras that make the children’s experiences in school so incredible - making learning more creative and fun, which the school budget simply doesn’t have the scope to pay for.
In recent years we have contributed towards: the music room; the ICT suite; outdoor areas; staging for productions; the sound system for the hall; sensory equipment; library and computing resources; planters for classrooms; internet safety workshops; and first aid sessions for the children.
We run a variety of events each year –the main ones being discos and the Summer and Christmas Fairs. We also hold smaller fundraising events (cake sales, second hand uniform sales, ice lolly sales etc.), and also get involved with community events (such as WitStock and Leaf Farm Open Day).
What can you do?
We are always looking for new members to join in to help drive future fundraising events and ideas for the coming year. We would love more people to join the team with whatever skills you have to offer - social media management (creating posts, events and responding to queries), designing flyers and posters, fundraising experience/lead generation, great local contacts for raffle and auction prizes, event planning, etc. etc. – we would love to hear from you all!
But you can get as involved as you want to be! If you can’t make the half-termly Friends meetings, there are plenty of opportunities to help out – such as selling cakes after school, baking cakes to sell, helping to set up events on the day, coming up with ideas for events and so on!
If you would like to offer any help, please email friends@chandlerjunior.school

School Meals
Children may choose to have a school lunch, or bring their own packed lunch from home (this must not contain nuts or nut products).
School lunch ordering
School lunches are pre-ordered online via Arbor, with a choice of three different options each day. To choose your child's lunch, go to Arbor, click on Quick Actions, Meals and then choose the current term. You should then be able to make your child's meal choices for each half term.
How to choose meals on Arbor
You will be able to book and change the lunch choices until 12pm the day before the meal.
If your child is having a packed lunch for any particular day, you do not need to do anything.
Payment
School lunches currently cost £2.90 per day (£14.50 per week).
Please pay on-line using Arbor. School meals must be paid for in advance and you can pay any amount (e.g. weekly, half termly, termly). Any credit left on the account will be rolled over to the next term.
Please contact the School Office should you be unable to pay online.
